issues.legal_issue: A tenancy of land belonging to a qualifying public-purpose trust is not heritable when the governing tenancy law excludes its inheritance provision from applying to that tenancy.
material_facts: The land belonged to a trust for an educational purpose or an institution for public religious worship, and the entire income from it was used for the trust’s purposes.
The trusts had received certificates confirming that they met the statutory conditions for the exemption.
The tenants or their predecessors held the lands as tenants and died; their heirs claimed to continue the tenancies.
The tenancy law’s provision governing inheritance by a tenant’s heirs did not apply to these tenancies.
The High Court upheld the view that the heirs could inherit under ordinary succession law, and the trusts appealed.
issues.conclusion: The heirs did not inherit the tenancies. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals and set aside the High Court’s judgments.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region) Act, 1958 governs the heritability of tenancies under that Act. Section 129(b) excludes its application to qualifying trust lands, and Section 37—which otherwise preserves tenant rights arising under other laws—is also excluded for those lands. The exclusion of Section 54 therefore excludes ordinary succession law as a basis for inheriting the tenancy. The Court rejected the contrary view in Khanqah-Kadria Trust (Wakf), Balapur v. Shevantabai wd/o Raoji Shivaji; it distinguished Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar because the present law expressly excluded the inheritance provision, and relied on the principle in Ratan Lal Adukia v. Union of India that a special code excludes general law on the subject.

rule.if: appeal_from_order_recognizing_heirs_tenancy and public_purpose_trust_land and income_fully_used_for_trust and qualification_certified and tenant_died and inheritance_rule_excluded_for_tenancy

predicates.appeal_from_order_recognizing_heirs_tena: An appeal challenges an order recognizing a deceased tenant’s heirs as entitled to continue the tenancy.
predicates.public_purpose_trust_land: The land belongs to a trust or institution holding it for an educational or public religious purpose.
predicates.income_fully_used_for_trust: The entire income from the land is used for the purposes of the trust or institution.
predicates.qualification_certified: An authorized official has certified, after inquiry, that the trust or institution meets the conditions for the relevant protection.
predicates.tenant_died: The tenant died while holding the land as a tenant.
predicates.inheritance_rule_excluded_for_tenancy: The governing tenancy law’s rule providing for inheritance of a tenancy does not apply to this tenancy.
predicates.tenancy_does_not_pass_to_heirs: The tenancy does not pass to the deceased tenant’s heirs.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges recognition of heirs’ tenancy and the land and income meet the stated public-purpose conditions, the qualification is certified, the tenant has died, and the inheritance rule is excluded, the tenancy does not pass to the heirs.
